id_and_class.summary: Jean-Paul Sartre holds that consciousness is a contentless, self-transcending activity, always directed at some object outside itself, that is also tacitly aware of itself without making itself an object. He calls this mode of being the for-itself, a ‘nothingness’ set against the dense, self-identical being of things (the in-itself). The ego is a construct of reflection, and consciousness itself is impersonal, translucent, and free.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Self-Aware Nothingness Directed at the World

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is the for-itself: pure, translucent directedness toward a world it is not, with no interior contents of its own, aware of itself pre-reflectively.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Sartre offers a phenomenological ontology, not a scientific theory. He distinguishes two modes of being, consciousness (for-itself) and things (in-itself), and treats consciousness as lived and embodied, never as a thing among things.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not addressed. Sartre characterizes the mode of being of consciousness without explaining its origin in matter.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Consciousness is exhaustively intentional, always consciousness of something. Subjectivity is its immediate, non-positional self-awareness: absorbed in counting cigarettes, I am tacitly conscious (of) counting without reflecting on it. Reflection, which makes consciousness its own object, is secondary.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Sartre's emptiness thesis denies that consciousness contains inner, quality-laden items. Phenomenal character belongs to the objects disclosed, which tends to dissolve the hard problem by relocating content to the world.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Two regions of being: the for-itself (consciousness as nothingness, lack, freedom) and the in-itself (inert, self-identical being). No ego inside consciousness.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Phenomenological description of lived experience. Consciousness is transparent to itself in its pre-reflective mode.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A world-directed act, its tacit self-awareness, and, in reflection, a constituted ego (the ‘I’). The lived field is shaped by negation, freedom, embodiment, affect, imagination, and exposure to the look of others.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal (as self-givenness); self-awareness; agency and freedom; intersubjectivity.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Nihilation: consciousness exists as a perpetual self-transcendence that never coincides with itself and discloses being as other than itself.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: The for-itself is never settled. It is a continual movement beyond itself toward objects and possibilities, which is why Sartre says it is ‘condemned to freedom’.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Nowhere inside. Consciousness is the situated point of view from which the world appears, with no private inner theater.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness discloses the world and grounds radical freedom; persons define themselves through projects and choices, and denying this freedom is bad faith.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Unity comes from consciousness's pre-reflective self-presence, not from an ego, which is constituted only in reflection.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Sartre rejects representational and container models: experience reveals worldly objects to an activity that is itself contentless.
core_claims_and_evidence: Consciousness contains no images, sensations, or mental contents; everything one is aware of is a transcendent object.
Every conscious state is aware of itself non-positionally, without taking itself as an object, and reflection presupposes this pre-reflective cogito.
The ego is a transcendent object constituted in reflection, so consciousness itself is impersonal and spontaneous.
As nothingness that never coincides with itself, the for-itself is radically free and responsible.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The claim that consciousness is fully transparent to itself sits uneasily with evidence of unconscious or opaque mental processes. Critics also doubt that non-positional self-awareness can be described without collapsing into a reflective relation (and its regress) or becoming too thin to explain anything.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Sartre does not connect the for-itself to brain processes, and his account addresses self-givenness more than sensory quality.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Internally unified around the for-itself / in-itself distinction. The emptiness thesis conflicts with representationalist philosophy of mind, while the pre-reflective cogito feeds directly into contemporary self-representational and phenomenological accounts.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Since there is no fixed human essence, persons create meaning through their own projects and choices and bear absolute responsibility for them.
